newsitem.title: USA: SEC recoups Gillette-Duracell deal insider profits.
newsitem.headline: SEC recoups Gillette-Duracell deal insider profits.

text.p: Federal regulators said Monday they won judgments of $2.77 million against traders who used inside information to profit on Duracell International Inc's merger with Gillette Co.

A U.S. District Court in New York ordered a Swiss firm, Lennox, S.A., to return $450,699 in illegal profits and "certain unknown purchasers" trading through a Bahamian account to return $603,275 and pay a $1.77 million fine, the Securities and Exchange Commission said.

Since the Bahamian account holders were unknown, the SEC said it would get part of its judgment from U.S. accounts containing the illicit proceeds that were frozen by the court when the agency filed its complaint on September 16.
The SEC's civil suit at the time accused unknown parties of buying 1,700 call options on Duracell in the days before its merger with Gillette was announced last September 12.

The call options, bought through accounts in Switzerland and the Bahamas that were designed to conceal the identities of the purchasers, rose as the price of Duracell's stock jumped 27 percent at the time of the merger announcement, the complaint said. The options were later sold for about $950,000.
Lennox consented to the court's judgment against it but did not admit or deny the allegations of the complaint, the SEC said.
The court also issued orders against the parties that could subject them to more severe penalties if they are found to violate federal securities laws in the future, the SEC said.
